name: HMMA Cylinder Head Machining Plant - Montgomery AL

fieldNotes.site: 260,000 sq ft cylinder-head machining plant ($388M, opened May 2019) — the 'third engine shop' on the HMMA campus, part of HMMA's 650K+ engines/yr operation. It is a component building INSIDE the larger 1,744-acre HMMA campus (same campus as idx 1), not a standalone site.
fieldNotes.buildingId: The exact building could not be uniquely distinguished from the other HMMA engine shops without floor-plan documentation. It is positively within the HMMA western engine-shop / component-plant cluster (centered ~32.2828,-86.3320). Center placed on that cluster.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Inherits HMMA campus access — controlled, numbered, guarded gates (web research confirms numbered gates, e.g. 'Gate 2'). The cylinder-head plant has no independent truck gate; inbound castings / outbound machined heads route through the shared campus gates.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true — shares the guarded HMMA campus perimeter (see idx 1).
fieldNotes.perimeter: Perimeter box = the full HMMA developed campus footprint (shared with idx 1), since this plant is a building within that campus.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: West engine-shop building face shows a dock bank with trailers backed in (~14 doors estimated for this building); the cylinder-head plant proper is a machining operation with modest dock needs. 10-25 band, low confidence.
fieldNotes.dropArea: A small trailer staging lot sits along the west engine-shop building face (~32.2825,-86.3330) holding ~20 trailers; modest drop activity. dropArea 0-10 for this building's own apron; campus-wide drop is much larger.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: true — building sits within the multi-building HMMA campus.
fieldNotes.dropYard: true at campus level (large HMMA SE drop yard); the cylinder-head plant itself has only a small adjacent trailer lot.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur into the developed campus footprint.
fieldNotes.note: This audit treats the cylinder-head plant as a campus-resident component building; its truck-yard profile is effectively the HMMA campus profile (idx 1) scoped to the western engine-shop cluster.
